approved: True-up Shortfall Levy (General) (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax and introduces new consumer protections.
The package would prohibit price exploitation on key goods like electricity and gas, and require suppliers to report cost savings to the ACCC.
Corporations that breach the price exploitation ban could face maximum penalties of 6,471 penalty units ($1,100,070), and individuals 1,295 penalty units ($220,150).
Prohibits entities from engaging in carbon-specific price exploitation on key goods after the carbon tax repeal.
Requires electricity and natural gas retailers and bulk synthetic greenhouse gas importers to provide substantiation statements to the ACCC on cost savings passed to customers.
Gives the ACCC monitoring powers to assess the effect of the carbon tax repeal on prices.
Requires electricity and natural gas retailers to prepare and communicate a statement to customers within 30 days after Royal Assent.
Imposes a penalty of 250 per cent of cost savings not passed through on suppliers that fail to pass through all savings.
Businesses that supply electricity, natural gas, or import bulk synthetic greenhouse gases, and their customers.

Moved a debate management motion to fast-track passage of the carbon tax repeal bills through the House together, arguing the September 2013 election gave the coalition a clear mandate, and recalled the 2010 pledge that there would be no carbon tax under a government Julia Gillard led.

Moved the second reading of the carbon tax repeal bills, saying Treasury modelling shows households will save an average of $550 a year, that the tax has cost $15 billion over two years, and citing an Independent Competition and Regulatory Commission estimate that electricity prices in the ACT will fall by 11.6 per cent once it is repealed.
